decisions.context: Forecasts must be reproducible for any past week, so the system needs to retain the inputs and their provenance. The design space supports preserving original data and tracing how it was processed.

alternatives.label: Traceable and preserved data
pros: Reproducibility: recover original inputs and processing history
cons: Weekly run stability: requires retained data and provenance

alternatives.label: Cataloged data
pros: Reproducibility: records dataset versions and metadata
cons: Past-week reproducibility: cataloging alone does not preserve original data

decisions.rationale: Past-week reproducibility decides the choice: retained, traceable inputs make historical reconstruction possible. Sources including “Architecting a Machine Learning Pipeline” describe provenance and data preservation; this adds storage and tracking work.
consequences: Retain immutable input snapshots and provenance.
Historical runs need references to the appropriate snapshots.

decisions.context: Reproducing a forecast requires more than retaining its data: the pipeline and experiment configuration must also be recoverable. The design space distinguishes this from versioning artifacts alone.

alternatives.label: Pipeline and experiment version control
pros: Reproducibility: compares and recovers configurations and runs
cons: Fast model iteration: adds versioning and tracking work

alternatives.label: Artifact version control
pros: Reproducibility: preserves model artifacts and dependencies
cons: Past-week reproducibility: omits pipeline and experiment history

decisions.rationale: Past-week reproducibility decides the choice because artifact versions alone do not capture how a forecast was produced. “Productionizing Machine Learning with a Microservices Architecture” and “AutoML” support versioning pipelines and experiments together.
consequences: Record pipeline and experiment versions with each run.
The team maintains more lifecycle metadata.

decisions.context: The system forecasts weekly demand, and workflow coordination in the design space requires an ingestion mechanism to be decided first. Batch ETL is a supported option for extracting and transforming records into features.

alternatives.label: ETL-based feature ingestion
pros: Weekly run stability: fits scheduled batch processing
cons: Past-week reproducibility: requires retained source snapshots

alternatives.label: Streaming feature ingestion
pros: Weekly run stability: continuously receives new records
cons: Weekly run stability: adds continuous ingestion operations

decisions.rationale: Weekly run stability decides the choice: batch extraction and transformation fits the stated weekly cadence. “Architecting a Machine Learning Pipeline” is evidence for this value; the brief does not call for continuous ingestion.
consequences: Schedule extraction and transformation ahead of the forecast run.
Preserve the ingested inputs for historical replay.

decisions.context: The system has a weekly run and new model ideas should reach production quickly without disrupting it. The design space presents an orchestrated pipeline as a repeatable alternative to manual script execution.

alternatives.label: Orchestrated ML pipeline
pros: Weekly run stability: connects repeatable workflow stages
cons: Fast model iteration: requires pipeline setup and upkeep

alternatives.label: Manual script-driven workflow
pros: Fast model iteration: permits direct manual experimentation
cons: Weekly run stability: depends on manual execution across stages

decisions.rationale: Weekly run stability decides the choice: an orchestrated pipeline makes stages repeatable, while manual execution leaves the weekly process dependent on operator actions. Sources including “Architecting a Machine Learning Pipeline” and “MLOps Principles” support pipeline coordination.
consequences: Represent preparation, training, and evaluation as ordered stages.
Pipeline changes require maintenance and validation.

decisions.decision: Promote model changes through staged automation
decisions.context: New model ideas should reach production quickly, but must not break the weekly run. Automated builds and tests with staged promotion provide a release path that checks changes before production.

alternatives.label: Commit-triggered staged release automation
pros: Fast model iteration: repository changes trigger delivery stages
cons: Weekly run stability: failed gates can delay promotion

alternatives.label: Unified release automation
pros: Fast model iteration: automates build, test, package, and release
cons: Weekly run stability: less explicit stage-by-stage promotion

decisions.rationale: Weekly run stability decides the choice: staged promotion allows automated delivery while retaining checks before production. “MLOps: Continuous delivery and automation pipelines in machine learning” supports commit-triggered builds and staged release; the trade-off is that gates can slow an individual change.
consequences: Changes pass automated build and test stages before production.
Promotion depends on passing release gates.

decisions.context: Model ideas need a reliable route to production that protects the weekly run. The design space describes held-out offline evaluation as a promotion check and threshold testing as a separate regression practice.

alternatives.label: Offline evaluation pipeline
pros: Weekly run stability: checks candidates before deployment
cons: Fast model iteration: evaluation adds a promotion step

alternatives.label: Metric-driven candidate model evaluation
pros: Fast model iteration: compares candidates on selected metrics
cons: Weekly run stability: does not alone define a held-out deployment check

alternatives.label: Previously-built-model diff testing
pros: Weekly run stability: compares a candidate with an existing model
cons: Fast model iteration: sources report maintenance difficulty

decisions.rationale: Weekly run stability decides the choice: evaluate candidates against held-out data before promotion. Sources including “MLOps Principles” and “MLOps: Continuous delivery and automation pipelines in machine learning” support offline evaluation; this adds a check to the delivery path.
consequences: Maintain held-out data and evaluation steps.

decisions.context: A three-person team owns the pipeline end to end and wants new ideas to reach production quickly. Short development cycles align with that goal, while the weekly run creates a need to validate changes as they progress.

alternatives.label: Lean iterative ML development
pros: Fast model iteration: delivers through short cycles
cons: Weekly run stability: frequent changes need validation

alternatives.label: Waterfall or V-model process
pros: Weekly run stability: defines sequential process stages
cons: Fast model iteration: sources reject heavyweight sequencing

decisions.rationale: Fast model iteration decides the choice: short cycles help the small team move model ideas forward. “MLOps Principles” and “MLOps: Continuous delivery and automation pipelines in machine learning” support iterative delivery; the cost is validating frequent changes against the weekly run.
consequences: Deliver model changes in small increments.
Keep release checks aligned with the weekly run.
